Sean / team — quick technical readout from initial triage: 

Summary:
- At 14:42 UTC we started a rolling kernel update across a subset of GPU servers in us-central; an operator-triggered kernel build (deploy ID: kernel-20280430-2) inadvertently changed a memory allocation path used by our KV cache eviction logic.
- Between 14:45–15:18 UTC multiple worker processes experienced KV cache mis-indexing which led to higher CPU contention (retries and synchronous cache refreshes) and duplicate partial generations for requests that hit the affected shard.
- Impact: increased 95th/99th token latency for ~8% of active requests in that region and ~0.6% of requests saw truncated/duplicated outputs.

Evidence / artifacts:
- KV cache eviction logs and stack traces (see attached: kv-eviction-log-snippet.txt)
- Request correlation (sampled IDs included) and timeline (incident-timeline.csv)

Immediate mitigations applied (15:22 UTC):
1) Rolled back kernel-20280430-2 on the affected nodes — latency returned to baseline by 15:28 UTC.
2) Disabled aggressive eviction policy for the KV cache and forced a full KV re-check across shards to clear mis-indexed entries.
3) Added a temporary routing rule to steer traffic away from the affected pool while we verify consistency.

Preliminary root cause: operator-triggered kernel update introduced a subtle change in memory alignment which exposed an existing race in our KV cache eviction code path. The race resulted in stale index references and synchronous fallback behaviors under load.

Proposed follow-ups and owners:
- Post-incident code fix for KV eviction race (owner: hannah_schmitt, ETA: 2028-05-06)
- End-to-end automated test for eviction alignment across kernels (owner: irene_choi, ETA: 2028-05-12)
- Improve rollout gating to run a lightweight KV-consistency probe pre-upgrade (owner: alex_martinez, ETA: 2028-05-09)
- Customer verification and credit proposal (owner: marissa_cole, ETA: 2028-05-03)

I'll prepare a concise technical appendix for the customer readout.

Hannah
Staff SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-05-02T18:00:00Z
Subject: Incident readout: April 30th inference interruption and remediation commitments

Tim —

Thank you for flagging this and for your patience while we completed our investigation. Below is a concise, customer-facing readout you can share with NebulaCorp leadership. I’ve attached a one-page readout (nebula-incident-readout-20280502.pdf) and the technical appendix for your engineers.

Executive summary:
- What happened: Between ~14:45 and 15:20 UTC on April 30th, a subset of servers in the us-central deployment experienced KV cache mis-indexing after a kernel update step. This led to increased token latencies and a small number of truncated/duplicated responses for live requests.
- Impact: Approximately 8% of active requests in the affected region saw a transient latency increase at the 95th/99th percentile; ~0.6% of requests experienced truncated or duplicated outputs. No user data was exposed or lost.
- Containment: We rolled back the kernel update and applied a temporary routing rule; normal performance returned by 15:28 UTC.

Root cause (plain language): An operator-initiated kernel deployment changed a memory alignment behavior that exposed a race condition in our KV cache eviction logic. Under load, the race caused stale references into the KV index and synchronous fallbacks that increased latency.

Immediate corrective actions taken:
- Rollback of kernel-20280430-2 on impacted nodes (15:22–15:28 UTC).
- Disabled aggressive eviction, forced a full KV re-check, and quarantined affected workers.
- Applied traffic steering away from the affected pool until consistency checks completed.

Planned remediation and timeline:
- Code-level fix for eviction race and additional unit tests (owner: Hannah Schmitt) — targeted 2028-05-06.
- KV-consistency probe to run as part of pre-upgrade smoke checks (owner: Irene Choi) — targeted 2028-05-09.
- Rollout gating changes to prevent operator-triggered kernel changes from reaching serving pools without KV probes (owner: Alex Martinez) — targeted 2028-05-12.
- Customer verification session: we propose a 30–45 minute technical sync next week to review the fix and validation plan (owner: Marissa Cole) — suggested window: 2028-05-04 through 2028-05-08.

Compensation / next steps:
- We recognize the impact and will propose a targeted service credit for the affected window. Marissa will follow up with a proposed credit and contract amendment for your review.

Attachments: nebula-incident-readout-20280502.pdf (customer-facing readout); technical appendix (kv-eviction-log-snippet.txt, incident-timeline.csv).

Please let me know if you want an expanded timeline or a dedicated review with our SRE/infra leads. We’re sorry for the disruption and appreciate your partnership as we improve our rollout safety.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive
